quote: It is a single family home. We do have a couple of trees. We we do have some and I am happy to take them out or part of them or cut them way back
stewart_read: Customer proactively volunteers to remove trees to improve solar viability — a strong buying signal showing she's already problem-solving toward a system, not just curious.
coaching_implication: Rep should have reflected this back explicitly ('that's great, that alone could open up meaningfully more roof space for panels') to reinforce her own motivation rather than just logging it as a note.

quote: There is. And anyone who makes the decisions.
stewart_read: The customer confirms there is a co-owner on the title who is also a decision-maker. This is a direct, unambiguous affirmative to the rep's co-owner question and triggers the spouse/co-owner inclusion protocol — the rep never asks who this person is or attempts to include them on the appointment.
coaching_implication: This is the single largest structural gap on the call. The rep should have asked 'Great, what's their name, and can we get them on the call with us Wednesday?' Instead the co-owner is never named or invited, leaving the appointment vulnerable exactly as the schema warns (SESSION20 negative example).

quote: Okay. No worries. If I surprise it, we can go ahead.
stewart_read: This follow-on line is garbled by the transcription but reads as the customer suggesting she can proceed and surprise the co-owner/decision-maker rather than requiring their attendance — it does not resolve whether the co-owner will actually be present, it just signals the customer's own workaround. It does not substitute for the rep confirming co-owner attendance per protocol.
alternative_hypothesis: The line could indicate the co-owner isn't needed for this appointment stage, which would reduce the severity of the miss — but nothing in the rep's next line tests or confirms this, so the ambiguity itself is the gap.
coaching_implication: Even if the customer self-volunteers a workaround, the rep should still ask a clarifying question ('would you like them included, or are you comfortable moving forward and looping them in after?') rather than let an ambiguous customer aside stand in for protocol.

quote: Yeah. So that's something a specialist can kinda go over with you once we get that design put together.
stewart_read: This is a clean, correct execution of the universal escape hatch — the rep does not guess at savings numbers and redirects to the specialist appropriately.
coaching_implication: Positive example worth reinforcing with the rep — this is the model response when pressed on numbers pre-design.

quote: $100,145 a month year round. Okay. That that will go up.
stewart_read: Customer gives a bill figure and immediately flags it's rising — a double signal (anchor + urgency) — but the rep only responds 'Right. Okay. So it's going up. Gotcha. Okay.' with no flip toward the value of locking in a solar payment before the increase.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to reflect rising bills as the reason to act now: 'that's exactly why people are moving now — lock in a flat solar payment before that keeps climbing.' The anchor and the flip were both available in the same breath and neither was used.

quote: Do you charge for the installation? So yeah. For the you or you rent them out?
stewart_read: Customer's third cost/ownership-structure question of the call. The rep admits a genuine knowledge gap rather than guessing, which is the correct move per schema (admit-and-redirect over fabricate), and defers to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read would flag this as scope creep risk, but the rep does not attempt to answer — they redirect immediately, so this is knowledge-gap handling done correctly, not creep.
coaching_implication: Reinforce the honest redirect, but flag for the manager that three separate cost questions from the same customer is a strong signal the closer needs to lead with pricing structure clarity early in their call.

quote: Were you able to receive that text message? Just wanna make sure you you have it. I got a text, and I'm getting a second. Oh, yes. I was able to get that text.
stewart_read: The rep confirms the text link arrived but the call ends without the actual bill photo being received — the appointment is booked contingent on a bill that has only been requested, not captured.
coaching_implication: This is fine procedurally (Ion allows booking pending bill), but the rep should explicitly note in the handoff/notes that the bill was not yet received by end of call, only the text link confirmed as delivered.
